title: The blush that gives us away
text: Charles Darwin called blushing {{1}} most peculiar of all human expressions. {{2}} makes it so peculiar is that the face betrays us at the very moment we would rather stay unread: it appears in exactly the social situations {{3}} we most want to disappear. Physically, blushing is simply {{4}} sudden rush of blood to the skin of the face, {{5}} is visible to everyone present, and the effect is so reliable {{6}} stage performers dread it. Worse, the fear of blushing tends to produce blushing, {{7}} if the body were determined to confirm the embarrassment. Psychologists still cannot fully explain {{8}} embarrassment floods the face rather than, say, the elbows, but the leading theory holds that the blush works as an involuntary apology, signalling that we know a social rule has been broken.
